title: The statistics predict mode reads
description: The statistics of one graph that kvevaluator predict reads to price plans without a store: one JSON file (kvevaluator graph-stats; our builder is python -m kvevaluator.predict.build_stats), with the anchor statistics in a second file read beside it (graph-stats --anchor-out; predict --anchor-stats). Every field is defined by the schema alone: no field names a dataset's labels or edge types, and a dataset declares only what its build passes (--anchor-labels, --date-axis). Nothing here depends on a layout: the statistics of each layout (kvevaluator tally) are a separate input. Check a file with python -m kvevaluator.predict.check_stats; predict refuses a file that lacks a field listed in `required`, and a rule refuses an absent optional field or entry it reads, by name, never a default. Terms. The owner of a list is the vertex whose edges the list stores: the source vertex for an out list, the destination for an in list. Level B is predict mode proper: it estimates from these whole-graph statistics alone, without knowing which vertex a query's parameter names. That vertex is the anchor (for example the person a query starts from). The anchor statistics describe one vertex; only the anchor level (level B plus them) reads them, never level B. A plan file may declare estimate_hints beside its question (size_biased: the edge types whose hop sources were reached through that edge type, so a hop over it takes a neighbour's degree; chase_root_ratio: the hops after a chase that read the chase root's conditional degree). A hint is coarse: it applies to every matching hop in the query. Each field says: x-tier, the kind of statistic (1: a count, one aggregate query; 2: a histogram or a richer statistic; anchor: one vertex's own statistic; file: the file's identity, written by the tool); x-per, what one entry is for; x-need, what in predict reads it; x-missing, what predict does when the field, or one of its entries, is absent; x-recipe, a query that computes it; x-written-by, which of our tools writes it.

type_counts.description: the number of vertices of each label
type_counts.x-per: vertex label (every label of the schema)
type_counts.x-missing: a label the file names elsewhere (an owners row, an end-label key) but does not count: refused at load; check_stats --schema refuses a file that lacks any label of the schema; any other missing label is refused when a plan reads it

edge_totals.description: the number of edges of each type
edge_totals.x-per: edge type (every edge type of the schema)
edge_totals.x-missing: an edge type the file names elsewhere but does not count: refused at load; check_stats --schema refuses a file that lacks any edge type of the schema; any other is refused when a plan reads it

distinct_src.description: the vertices with at least one out-edge of the type: the owners of its out lists
distinct_src.x-need: always (a mean degree is edges / owners)
distinct_src.x-missing: a missing edge type is refused when a plan reads it

distinct_dst.description: the vertices with at least one in-edge of the type: the owners of its in lists
distinct_dst.x-missing: a missing edge type is refused when a plan reads it

owners.description: per edge type and direction, the owners of its lists by the owner's label, and their edges: one row per (edge type, direction, owner label) with at least one owner; a label that owns no list of E in that direction has no row (not a row of zeros)
owners.x-need: every KV step (predict --plans, --accuracy); a hop whose consumers read its rows as one label (far_label_consumer) keeps that label's rows' share of the far end's edges. The share stands in for the far labels the hop's sources do not hold (LDBC: cities hold no messages): the hop's own rows are scaled, so where the sources' lists really hold several labels its edges read are under by that share
owners.x-missing: every KV step is refused, the field named

sizes.description: bytes and counts of the graph's content, layout-free: {"content": {key: {"b": bytes, "u": units}}}. Bytes are content bytes: a string's length in characters, an integer 8, a boolean 1, a float 0, a bytes value its raw length, a list or an object the sum of its members. Four kinds of key: prop|L|p, a property of a label: u = the vertices of L with a value for p, b = those values' total bytes (LDBC sf0.1, prop|Person|id: u 1528, b 12224, so 8 B per value); tok|L|p, an indexed property: u = its index tokens (one per vertex of L with a value), b = the tokens' total length, each value written as text (tok|Post|creationDate: u 135701, b 1764113, so 13.0 characters per token, a date in milliseconds); eprop|E, an edge type: u = the edges of E, b = their edge properties' total bytes (eprop|isLocatedIn: u 296227, b 0, no edge properties); esrc|E|L and edst|E|L: the key says label L sits at the source (esrc) or destination (edst) end of E; u = the edges of E with an L vertex at that end, b = 0 (esrc|isLocatedIn|Post: u 135701, b 0). Every property a vertex record carries has a prop key: the declared ones and the dataset's own id (prop|L|id, an int). A missing value is no value: null, or the empty string for a property the dataset schema declares nullable (a store that keeps "" for a missing value, as Dgraph does). b may come from a sample (a share of the elements, as PostgreSQL's ANALYZE does): b = the sample's bytes per element times u; the share goes in sizes.sample (0 < share <= 1; absent: every element measured). u is always exact: load checks the per-day and per-value counts against it. Predict reads prop's b and u, the presence of the esrc and edst keys (not their b or u), and the edge type an eprop key names; it does not read tok's b and u.
sizes.x-per: label and property; edge type; edge type, end and label
sizes.x-need: always (the esrc / edst keys give a hop's starting population; prop gives a property read's hits and bytes)
sizes.x-missing: a missing prop|L|p key is refused by name where a step reads it (graph-stats writes one per declared property, u = 0 when no vertex holds it), and check_stats --schema finds it first; load refuses a file whose edge type has edges but no esrc or edst key
sizes.x-recipe: count(n.p), sum(size(n.p)) per label (the bytes from a sample); the end labels from the schema

ndv.description: the distinct values of a property that an equality index read filters on; key L|p
ndv.x-per: label and property (each one a plan reads with read_index_eq)
ndv.x-missing: a key the file lacks is refused when a plan reads it
ndv.x-recipe: MATCH (n:L) RETURN count(DISTINCT n.p) (an approximate count is fine)
ndv.x-written-by: graph-stats, per indexed property of the schema

top_values.description: the most common values of an indexed property, each with its vertices: {"k": how many the file keeps, "holders": the vertices whose record carries the property (null included: the population ndv counts), "values": [[value, vertices], ...] by vertices, then value}; key L|p, as ndv. Tier 2 keeps 1,000 (every value when there are no more), tier 1 the first 10. An equality on an indexed property (an index read; a filter's eq, in, ne) has a listed value's count as its rows, any other value the rest spread evenly: (holders - the listed counts) / (ndv - listed). Several eq, in or ne fields of one label in one filter keep the smallest field's share, not their product: they are taken as correlated (rule value_share_correlated; JOB's info with info_type_id)
top_values.x-per: label and property (each non-date one the schema indexes; no plan reads a date by equality)
top_values.x-need: an equality on an indexed property: an index read (read_index_eq), a filter's eq, in or ne
top_values.x-missing: a key the file lacks is refused when a plan reads it. Load refuses holders above the label's type count, a count <= 0, counts summing above the holders, and more values than ndv
top_values.x-recipe: MATCH (n:L) RETURN n.p, count(*) ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 10; the holders: MATCH (n:L) RETURN count(n) over the vertices whose record carries p
top_values.x-written-by: graph-stats, per indexed property of the schema

top_degrees.description: per owner label, edge type, direction and indexed property of that label, the values whose vertices own the most edges there: {"k": how many the file keeps (10, both tiers), "owners": every vertex of the label with an edge of that type and direction, holding the property or not (read only by load's check owner_values <= owners), "owner_values": the distinct values of the owners holding the property, "edges": the edges of the owners holding the property only, "values": [[value, edges], ...] by edges, then value; a value several owners hold sums their edges}; key L|E|dir|p, dir out or in. A hop straight from an equality index read on L reaches a listed value's edges, any other value the rest spread over the other owners' values: (edges - the listed) / (owner_values - listed)
top_degrees.x-per: owner label, edge type, direction and indexed property (every declared end of an edge type, each non-date property the schema indexes on that label)
top_degrees.x-need: a hop (read_neighbors, out or in) whose sources are an equality index read (read_index_eq with a value) on the hop's source-side label
top_degrees.x-missing: a key the file lacks is refused when a plan reads it. Load refuses owners above the label's type count, owner_values above owners, an edge count <= 0, edges summing above the total, and more values than owner_values
top_degrees.x-recipe: MATCH (n:L)-[:E]->() WITH n.p AS v, count(*) AS d RETURN v, d ORDER BY d DESC LIMIT 10 (<-[:E]- for in); owners, owner_values and edges over the vertices with such an edge
top_degrees.x-written-by: graph-stats, per declared end and indexed property of the schema

value_range.description: the least and greatest value of each int property the schema declares, [least, greatest], or null when no element holds it; key prop|L|p for a vertex label's property, eprop|E|p for an edge type's. A range filter reads the per-value counts (int_values); this is their flat form's span, and null means the filter keeps no row
value_range.x-per: int property of a vertex label or an edge type (every one of the schema)
value_range.x-need: a range filter (lt, le, gt, ge against a value) on an int property: of the rows' one label, of each label of a set of several (weighted by the labels' type counts, a concat's sides' rows, or an unlabelled hop's far-end shares), or of the edges the rows came through; int_values' flat form
value_range.x-missing: a missing entry is refused by name when a filter reads it; check_stats --schema finds it first. Load refuses a key that is not prop|counted label|property or eprop|counted edge type|property, and a value that is not [least <= greatest] or null
value_range.x-recipe: MATCH (n:L) RETURN min(n.p), max(n.p); MATCH ()-[e:E]->() RETURN min(e.p), max(e.p)

int_values.description: the elements per integer value of an int property: {"first": the least value, "counts": one count per value up to the greatest, 0 where none holds it}, the same form as date_days (per value instead of per day); key prop|L|p or eprop|E|p, as value_range. Written for a property whose values span at most 1,000,000 integers. A range filter's rows are the counts of the values it covers, over the label's type count (or the edge type's edges)
int_values.x-per: int property of a vertex label or an edge type
int_values.x-need: a range filter on an int property (as value_range says)
int_values.x-missing: refuses; the flat form is an even spread over value_range: first = the least value, one count per value, each the holders / the values. Load refuses an entry that does not run from value_range's least to its greatest, a negative count, a vertex property's counts that do not sum to sizes.content's u, and an edge property's above the edge type's edges
int_values.x-recipe: MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.p IS NOT NULL RETURN n.p, count(*) ORDER BY n.p

degree_given_via.description: per label and per ordered pair of its distinct degrees (via, target; each E|dir with dir out, in or both, the label's degree_hist keys): a histogram over the via degree, one row per bucket (degree_hist's buckets): [bucket, vertices, summed via degree, summed target degree]; bucket 0 holds the label's vertices with no via edge and their summed target degree; a row with no vertices may be left out; key L|E|dir>E2|dir2
degree_given_via.x-need: optional: the vertices a multi-hop read reaches (a vertex reached through edge type A is not an average vertex)
degree_given_via.x-missing: the whole-graph mean degree (a coarser rule)
degree_given_via.x-recipe: per vertex both degrees; GROUP BY bucket(degree A) (degree_hist's): count, sum(degree A), sum(degree B)

degree_hist.description: per label, edge type and direction: the label's vertices by their degree, one row per bucket: [bucket, vertices, summed degree, summed squared degree]; bucket 0 holds the vertices with no such edge; a degree d >= 1 is in bucket floor(log2 d) + 1, its bit length (d = 1 in bucket 1, 2-3 in 2, 4-7 in 3). A row with no vertices may be left out (graph-stats writes bucket 0 always). Rows for every label that owns at least one list of E in that direction (none for a label that owns none); key L|E|dir, dir out, in, or both (out + in, on a label that owns lists in both directions of E)
degree_hist.x-need: a hop over an edge type the plan declares size-biased (a neighbour's degree, sum(d^2) / sum(d); neighbor_degree_ratio may stand in), a write's list read (the size of the endpoint's list: the mean, or the size-biased mean sum(d^2) / sum(d) when the write picks an existing edge's endpoint), and the share of lists past a Condensed split
degree_hist.x-missing: refuses; the flat form is every owner at the mean degree, from the owners row: [[0, vertices - owners, 0, 0], [bucket of m, owners, edges, edges * m]], m = edges / owners. Load refuses rows that disagree with tier 1: the vertices against type_counts, the summed degree against edge_totals and the owners row, a sum of squares below (sum d)^2 / owners, a 'both' row whose summed degree is not the label's out plus in, a bucket that is not a whole number. A read of an edge type with edges and no row for any label refuses with the flat rows
degree_hist.x-recipe: per vertex its degree (0 included); GROUP BY bucket (0 for degree 0, else floor(log2(degree)) + 1): count, sum(degree), sum(degree^2)

neighbor_degree_ratio.description: a neighbour's degree over the mean degree: sum(d^2) / sum(d) over edges / owners, for the owners of E's lists in direction dir; key E|dir. 1 is the flat form (every owner at the mean). Not cond_degree: that ratio divides by the mean over every vertex of the end labels, owners or not
neighbor_degree_ratio.x-need: a hop over an edge type the plan declares size-biased, when degree_hist has no row for it
neighbor_degree_ratio.x-missing: refuses (when degree_hist has no row either); the flat form is 1. Load refuses a value below 1 or an edge type edge_totals does not count
neighbor_degree_ratio.x-recipe: per owner its degree d: sum(d^2) / sum(d), divided by count(*) / count(DISTINCT owner)
neighbor_degree_ratio.x-written-by: none (a user's file; graph-stats writes degree_hist)

date_days.description: the vertices per day of a date property; key L|p: {first_day (days since 1970-01-01), counts}; one entry per date property the dataset schema declares on a label, when at least one vertex holds it; a day is the UTC day, floor(milliseconds / 86,400,000)
date_days.x-need: date windows, date-index reads and the ranked date-index walk (their span, populated days and recency), and filters that bound a date property (the date_filter rule)
date_days.x-missing: refuses; the flat form is an even spread over the property's dates: {first_day: the earliest, counts: one per day to the latest, each u / the days}, u from sizes.content prop|L|p. Load refuses counts whose sum is not that u (exactly: unrounded, or the remainder on one day). A date filter on a property the dataset schema declares a date refuses too; a filter on another field keeps the filter rule

date_axis.description: the labels and date property a date rule reads when its step names none: {labels, prop}; declared by the dataset's build (--date-axis). A user who gives only data declares it from the plans: the labels and date a date window means when it names none (LDBC: the messages, Post and Comment, by creationDate); the labels' order does not matter
date_axis.x-need: a date rule whose step names no labels or prop, and a date filter's span without a per-day histogram
date_axis.x-missing: refused by name where a rule needs it

forest.description: per edge type whose source labels are all among its destination labels and whose every source has exactly one such edge (a parent pointer): {sources, depth_sum (hops to the chain's root, summed over the sources), source_labels, labels}; every edge type that passes the rule, whether or not a plan chases it (LDBC: replyOf, isSubclassOf, isPartOf)
forest.x-per: edge type that is a forest
forest.x-need: optional: a chase's depth and a closure's size (1 + the mean depth over the forest's labels)
forest.x-recipe: a recursive query over the edge type

recency.description: per anchor label L, edge type E, direction dir and date property p: for each (E, dir) whose lists L owns and whose far-end labels do not include L and all declare p (LDBC's Person: hasCreator in, hasMember in, hasModerator in, likes out, by creationDate; not knows, whose far end is Person), over the vertices of L with a neighbour there: the days back from the far end's last day to the k-th newest neighbour (k = 1, 10, 20; the far end's span when fewer): {vertices, span, last_day, mean {k}, deciles {k: 11 values}}; span = the far labels' last day - their first day + 1 (both days counted), last_day their last; key L|E|dir|p. Built only for the --anchor-labels labels: it is read only for a bound vertex's neighbours
recency.x-per: anchor label, edge type, direction, date property
recency.x-need: optional: the ranked date-index walk over the anchor's neighbours (read_top_k_by_index), at level B (the mean and deciles)
recency.x-recipe: per anchor vertex, rank its neighbours by p

burstiness.description: how far a ranked walk down p's date index goes to find an owner's k newest neighbours (k = 20), over how far it goes when the neighbours are spread evenly over the index; key E|dir|p, for each edge type and direction whose far-end labels all hold a sorted index on p. Per owner o of an E list in direction dir (every owner label) with n >= 4k neighbours: crossed = the index entries on days newer than its k-th newest neighbour's day, plus half of that day's; even = min(N, k N / n), N the index's entries; the value is the mean of crossed / even weighted by n, and 1 when no owner has 4k neighbours. It is built at k = 20 and read at the walk's own k. An owner with fewer than 4k is left out: the even spread k N / n is then above N / 4, near all of N as n nears k, so the ratio measures the owner's size (about 0.5 whatever the dates), not where its k-th newest sits. 1 is the flat form (an even spread); above 1, an owner's neighbours are older than the index's newest (a person's messages come in bursts)
burstiness.x-need: the ranked date-index walk (read_top_k_by_index) over the far ends of a hop (its vids reached through read_neighbors and the ops that keep rows), except the anchor's own neighbours when their recency is read: the entries crossed are b k N / candidates. A walk with no hop behind it (a label scan) is the index itself: no entry
burstiness.x-missing: refuses; the flat form is 1. Load refuses a key that is not edge type|out or in|property of a counted edge type, and a value below 0
burstiness.x-recipe: per owner with at least 4k neighbours, rank them by p, newest first; the k-th's day d: count the index entries with p on a day after d, plus half of day d's

degree_by_far_label.description: the list a new edge from a far-end label grows: key O|E|dir|F, for each declared pair of ends (owner label O, far label F) of edge type E in direction dir (out: O is the source). Value [n, sum]: n the E edges in direction dir between an O and an F vertex; sum the summed degree (O's E list in dir) of the O vertex each of them lands on, sum over owners o of n_F(o) x d(o). sum / n is the list size a new edge from an F vertex meets, an owner drawn by its edges from F (a new Post's isLocatedIn lands on a Country's message list, a new Person's on a City's list). With one declared far label it is degree_hist's sum d^2 / sum d. The flat form (tier 1's, kvevaluator.predict.tier1), from counts alone: n the owners row's edges of O|E|dir split over the far labels it declares in proportion to each one's vertex count (type_counts), every owner at the mean degree m = edges / owners (degree_hist's flat row): [n, n x m]
degree_by_far_label.x-per: owner label, edge type, direction, far label
degree_by_far_label.x-need: an insert_edge into a Condensed list (the list read and rewritten) whose owner is neither created in the request nor an anchor
degree_by_far_label.x-missing: refuses; the flat form is [n, n x m], n the owners row's edges split over the declared far labels by vertex count, m = edges / owners. Load refuses a key that is not owner label|edge type|out or in|far label of a counted edge type, a value that is not [n, sum] with sum >= n, and n summed over an edge type and direction above its edge total
degree_by_far_label.x-recipe: per edge (s, t) of E: add 1 to n of s's label|E|out|t's label and of t's label|E|in|s's label, and the degree of s (of t) to their sums, the degrees those of the whole graph

cond_degree.description: per ordered pair of distinct degrees (via E|dir, target E2|dir2; dir out, in or both), pooled over every label that holds both: over the vertices with a via edge, the target degree's mean weighted by the via degree, sum(via x target) / sum(via), divided by the target's population mean (E2's edges over the vertices of the labels at that end; for both, the out mean plus the in mean), rounded to 4 places; key E|dir>E2|dir2 (no label). For a forest F: chase-root|F>E2|dir2, the target degree of the root each chase from a source of F lands on, weighted by the sources landing on it, over the same population mean; one key per degree that any label of F has. A pair whose via sum or population mean is 0 has no key
cond_degree.x-need: optional: a hop from a set reached through an edge (the frontier's degree); a hop after a chase reads the root's only when the plan declares chase_root_ratio
cond_degree.x-recipe: per vertex its degrees; per (via, target): sum(via x target) / sum(via) over the vertices with a via edge, over the target's edges / the vertices at its end

anchor_degrees.description: one vertex's degree per edge type and stored direction; key: the vid, then E|dir (non-zero degrees only; a vertex with no edge has an empty entry). Written for every vertex of the labels a plan's bound vertex has (--anchor-labels; LDBC: Person), or for the vids a study's params bind (--anchor-vids; JOB, LinkBench). In the anchor file (--anchor-out), read with predict --anchor-stats
anchor_degrees.x-need: never at level B; only at the anchor level (a write's list sizes for the bound vertex; a read's neighbours of a vid the plan names)
anchor_degrees.x-missing: the vertex is unknown: knows_out / knows_in / person_msgs, else the whole-graph mean
anchor_degrees.x-written-by: graph-stats --anchor-labels / --anchor-vids (graph_stats.json; kvevaluator predict takes it as --anchor-stats)

anchor_recency.description: per recency key, one anchor vertex's own days back to its 1st, 10th and 20th newest neighbour; key: the recency key, then the vid (hex16). A vertex of the anchor labels with no neighbour there has no row and walks the whole span
anchor_recency.x-need: never at level B; only at the anchor level
anchor_recency.x-missing: level B's recency mean and deciles

anchor_far_labels.description: one anchor vertex's edges per edge type and stored direction, split by the far end's label; key: the vid, then E|dir, then the far label. Only for an (E, dir) whose far end declares two or more labels (LDBC: a Person's hasCreator in, Posts and Comments). Written for the same vertices as anchor_degrees, in the anchor file
anchor_far_labels.x-need: never at level B; only at the anchor level (the label mix of a set read from the bound vertex: which labels' props or lists a step reads)
anchor_far_labels.x-missing: the far end's label mix of the whole graph (owners)

dataset.description: the dataset's name (--dataset): the statistics' owner, and the key of its extension

extension.description: a dataset's own fields, keyed by the dataset's name, defined by its own schema (python/kvevaluator/datasets/<name>/statistics/schema.json); kept opaque by every reader. No dataset has one: every field a rule reads is in this contract
extension.x-need: none today: a rule that needs one reads it by name and is refused without it

provenance.description: the file's identity: schema_hash (the hash of the dataset schema; predict refuses another), sf (the scale; predict refuses another), and how the file was made (the binary, the commit)
provenance.x-need: always (checked against --schema and the request's scale)

schema_hash.description: the schema hash graph-stats wrote (predict refuses another)
schema_hash.x-need: always (checked against --schema and the anchor file's)

samples.description: planned, not read yet: a sample of owners (for p% of the owners, each one's full sorted list of target ids per edge type and direction, and its property bytes); it would give the id gaps and id order that the layout statistics need
samples.x-need: planned: the layout statistics without a full pass
samples.x-recipe: MATCH (a)-[:E]->(b) WHERE hash(id(a)) % 100 < p RETURN id(a), collect(id(b))
